text.p: Flooding, mudslides, sinkholes, and other storm-related problems have battered the Pacific Northwestern US. Drier and cooler weather in the coming days will be more favorable as flood waters will begin to recede and clean up operations can commence.

Tropical Cyclone 15S (Rachel) is moving west-southwestward in the Timor Sea with top winds of 35 mph. Slow intensification is expected as the storm continues on its track. This system will become an increasing threat to shipping over the next 24-72 hours. Tropical Cyclone 14S has formed east of Madagascar in the South Indian Ocean near 14s/55e. TC 14S is moving west-southwest at 7 mph and will further intensify this period, likely becoming a bigger threat to shipping late in the period. Tropical Cyclone 16P, with 40 mph winds will intensify north and west of Espiritu Santo Island this period as it tracks southwestward well north of New Caledonia. Shipping will be under increasing risk from this system over the next 48 hours.

A storm in southwest Europe is causing rain in Portugal and Spain with rain, snow and freezing rain in south France. This storm will continue during the next 24 hours. We can expect to see heavy rain in Portugal and Spain that may change to snow is in the north. Snow and rain could also be quite heavy in south France and north Italy. Strong winds in the western Mediteranean sea may cause problems for shipping and boating as the storm strengthens during Friday.
